correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs all quantifiers for odd prime p and d>=2. Restriction to the affine difference span is exact; the one-dimensional local transform has at most two zeros by the prime-order Fourier-minor theorem; the two-dimensional local transform has at most two zeros because |a+b zeta^x|=|c| is a line-circle intersection condition and y is then unique. Explicit nonzero coefficient triples realize 0, 1 and 2 zeros on every fixed support. Exact cyclotomic checks corroborate the local claims for p=3,5,7,11.

value.rationale: Three-point supports are the first odd-prime finite-vector-space case with two affine geometry types. A complete fixed-support spectrum is stronger and more reusable than a minimum uncertainty bound: it identifies exactly how many annihilator cosets can vanish, shows every option occurs on every support, and yields a closed five-value spectrum in all dimensions. The noncollinear stratum is especially informative because it quantifies the spectral penalty for leaving an affine line.
